# Decisions

- **2026-10-09 — Computer-use v0 priority:** Henry said, “lets try to get a v0 computer use merged into the v3 admin agent today, with the ability to view the computer in real time. i think that would be incredibly nice. thanks.” The active priority is a v0 computer-use integration into the Admin-v3 agent with real-time computer viewing; completion is not yet recorded.

- **2026-10-09 — Luna judge configuration:** Henry said, “1. yes, luna as the default model is a good idea\n2. yes, i agree with this, we can do one run for each segment, lets do it.” Luna is the default judge model, with one judge run for each segment.

- **2026-10-09 — v3 tool-use visibility:** Henry clarified, “thats really it. the v3 agent also doesn't show tool use”. Tool-use activity is absent from both the Admin-v3 copied transcript UI and the customer v3 agent; it is not an Admin-v3-only projection or theming defect.

> Supersession status (2026-10-09): the prior decision described below is **Superseded**.

- **2026-10-09 — Orchard St Homecare caregiver-simulator direction:** Henry said, “i think we should think about this in more of a \"demo to new customers\" view. but yes, ideally we would want:\n1. 99% response and 95% \"yes\" (or even a couple yes's per outreach would be beneficial)\n\ndailys runs are not a high priority right now, its more about demo value, and making the simulated caregivers act accordingly”. The active direction is customer-demo value rather than daily automation: simulated caregivers target approximately 99% response and 95% yes outcomes, with at least a couple of yes replies per outreach beneficial, and caregiver behavior is aligned to convincing demos.

- **2026-10-09 — Orchard simulator audit and refactor goals:** Henry's direction supersedes the audit's unresolved target-rate and daily-cadence questions. The refactor remains read-only planning at this stage, with demo behavior, caregiver acceptance, natural responses, and lower cost as the primary goals; daily runs are not a current priority.

- **2026-10-09 — Sandbox-pool plan discussion format and deslop work:** Henry said, “ok lets just talk through the sandbox pool plan, i dont really like reading huge markdown files. can we also start the deslop pr #6 and #7.” Henry prefers discussing the sandbox-pool plan conversationally rather than reading a large Markdown plan, and requested initiation of Admin-v3 deslop PRs 6 and 7. No completion or implementation result for these requests is recorded in this transcript range.

- **2026-10-09 — Persistent-sandbox design discussion format:** Henry said, “sorry can we talk through the persistent sandboxes design doc again, thanks”. Henry prefers discussing the persistent-sandbox design document conversationally rather than reviewing it only as a large document.

- **2026-10-09 — Admin-v3 subagent architecture:** Henry said, “i think having it be a custom model loop written inside the browse tool is a little weird no? like the idea i have is that we generalize subagents, and then we have different \"profiles\" for popular types of subagents: investigation, browse, etc that can have a pre-defined set of pre-loaded tools. i think that might be the best way i can think about it.” The active direction is generalized subagents with named profiles such as investigation and browse, each with a predefined tool set, rather than a browse-specific model loop.

- **2026-10-09 — General subagents and write approvals:** Henry approved allowing the Admin-v3 agent to spawn general subagents with essentially all tools, alongside specialized profiles. The rationale was that the orchestrator can offload heavier investigation and analysis while continuing to coordinate, and organization-scoped Modal sandboxes give subagents access to the same workspace. Henry selected option B for writes and approval-requiring work: the orchestrator is the judge for whether a subagent proposal is approved, rather than mounting a subagent approval card in the main chat without sufficient user context.

- **2026-10-08 — Admin-v3 persistent workspace plan:** The approved plan uses Modal Volume v2 after a staging canary and restore drill, with S3 as the recovery source because Volume v2 is beta and lacks transactions. Initial Admin-v3 resources are 2 CPU, 4 GiB memory, a 30-minute idle timeout, a 30-minute command maximum, and at most two concurrent commands in a fixed pool. A root workspace and its child agents share one mutation lease, unrelated roots do not block one another, and an idle Sandbox older than 20 hours is replaced immediately before dispatch. The physical cross-root shared area remains unexposed initially. Dedicated-bucket daily checkpoints have 90-day retention, and the cutover excludes Orchard sandbox files. The `codebase` tool is retired after staging clone/pull validation, while egress metadata logging is deferred. Admin-v3 uses `block_network=False` without an outbound domain allowlist; customer `OrgSandboxPool` retains `block_network=True`.

- **2026-10-09 — Admin-v3 UI assessment:** Henry said, “another thing, the new v3 ui is complete slop.” This records a negative user assessment of the new v3 UI following completion of the copied transcript UI work.
